long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Brooklyn public housing, Howard Schultz became the first in his family to graduate from college. His father's workplace injury shaped his view of employment before he became Starbucks' modern-day founder. Hurt and left without income or health cover, his father showed Schultz the insecurity of low-paid work. He later offered part-time Starbucks staff health insurance and stock options, linking the company's growth to benefits rarely available in retail.

With his wife Sheri, Schultz later established the Schultz Family Foundation to widen access to opportunity. Its work concentrates on helping young people move into adulthood and employment, while programmes also assist military veterans entering civilian careers. The foundation's Veteran Transition Partnership provides junior enlisted service members with career navigation and employment support before and after they leave active duty.

uncertainties.detail: Starbucks created the fortune and Schultz still holds a material stake, but he left its board and executive leadership in 2023. Current official sources instead describe family investments, founder mentoring and Maveron, and 2026 reporting confirms a family office. Finance & Investments is selected for his present identifiable private-business interests, while the family office's portfolio values and allocation remain private.

Founder precisely describes Schultz's historical relationship to Starbucks, but Investor better matches the separately selected current Finance & Investments interests. Family office principal is a plausible alternative; it is not selected because current public evidence confirms the office's existence without establishing that Schultz personally directs its day-to-day allocation.

Forbes' profile was last updated on 10 March 2026 and still lists Seattle, while Schultz's LinkedIn statement and Bloomberg reporting one day later say that he and Sheri moved to Miami. The existing system stores only United States as the main residence country, which remains correct and is not reproposed.

The LinkedIn profile is active and independently connected to a current first-person statement. X and Instagram are supported as official personal accounts by independent or government evidence but appear dormant legacy profiles; they are proposed with that caveat. Focused research did not support namesake TikTok or YouTube accounts.

HowardSchultz.com redirects to the joint emes project organisation and no longer functions as a distinct personal biography or publishing site. It is therefore not proposed as a Personal Website; the exact Schultz Family Foundation biography is proposed as a Company Website instead.

The owner input links Schultz to the 100-metre Pi. Independent n-tv reporting links the same former Starbucks chief executive to 100-metre Project 824, strengthening identity resolution. Vessel evidence is excluded from both biographies and from all wealth classifications.

Strong first-party and independent sources establish Schultz's public-housing upbringing, first-generation college status and household insecurity, while Starbucks documents that he raised capital for Il Giornale before acquiring its assets. The reviewed sources do not itemise every investor contribution or Schultz's exact personal cash commitment, but they identify no inherited capital or family-business platform; the independent-start classification therefore does not rely on absence of evidence alone.

No secondary nationality, suffix, formal title or stable secondary residence country was established. The input's American nationality, United States birth and residence countries, male gender and living status remain consistent. The stale age fields, death fields, notes and system-managed fields are not proposed.
